body:
## Why

The merged [#38 / PR #45](https://github.com/grove/proofline/pull/45) medium/high pilot finally exposed the problem Proofline is meant to address: **three of six completed, source-audited coding implementations omitted original user obligations despite passing the selected original repository tests**. They missed requested documentation or installation behavior. The experiment then stopped on a native timeout, so it did **not** establish a medium/high winner or any benefit from guidance.

Earlier [#32](https://github.com/grove/proofline/issues/32) and [#34](https://github.com/grove/proofline/issues/34) studies encountered correctness ceilings on smaller tasks. We should now test **the smallest plausible intervention**: can a brief, source-grounded acceptance checklist help a capable coding agent deliver the *whole* user request, without extra orchestration or burdensome planning?

**Question:** Does one concise acceptance checklist supplied to Luna:medium before implementation increase independently correct *complete* deliveries enough to justify its entire preparation and execution overhead, compared with Luna working normally?

## Small, frozen two-arm comparison

- Choose **four fresh, real, substantial coding requests** with exact original issue/request text and reproducible base commits: multiple modules where warranted, preservation/compatibility obligations, negative cases, and some user-facing documentation/installation expectations. Prefer natural ongoing work; do not create artificial product requirements just to manufacture defects. **Do not reuse exposed #16/#32/#34/#38 task/solution/oracle pairs** or choose tasks after inspecting candidate outcomes.
- **A — ordinary Luna:** GPT-6 Luna:medium receives the complete original request and ordinary allowed repository context and tools; it implements and self-checks normally.
- **B — checklist + Luna:** Identical Luna:medium, starting bytes, full original request, tools, ordinary tests and **matched total per-assignment time budget**. Additionally receives one brief **pre-frozen source-grounded acceptance checklist** before starting implementation. No extra planning agent, Sol, mandatory Proofline step, reviewer, retry or privileged tests.
- The checklist is **short and task-oriented**, derived only from the original request: outcome commitments, exclusions/constraints, compatibility, negative behavior, docs/installation and any material assembly/integration checks. Source-link each item to exact request text; explicitly label ambiguity rather than inventing a requirement. Target at most ~8–12 meaningful items or a single page. **The checklist does not narrow or replace the original request, reveal hidden oracle values, prescribe the implementation, or make a quality/approval claim.**
- Freeze **before live dispatch**: all four tasks and base commits, checklist texts and source citations, an independently reviewed source-faithful grading plan with permitted alternatives, hidden execution probes, normal public tests, candidate/control fixtures, models/reasoning, prompts, run order, exact budgets, every assigned cell and stop rules. Independently qualify reference/alternative/defective controls through the existing [#36 preflight](https://github.com/grove/proofline/issues/36). A passing regression suite is not independent whole-request success.
- Run **all eight matched assignments (4 × 2)** in a balanced order, with no cherry-picking or outcome-driven task swaps, and one initial coding attempt per assignment. If an actual native access/isolation/budget problem requires stopping, preserve every assigned slot as completed, unavailable, or unexecuted; don't retry, resume a failed attempt, change the corpus, or call the comparison complete.
- Use the **existing native evaluation/snapshot/receipt/accounting utilities** from #38 only as needed; a small fixture/adapter is preferable to a new runner framework. Evaluation must not change `proofline.py check`, install new model routing, or make Intentline a required service.

## Source fidelity, fairness and costs

- Every worker gets **the complete unchanged original request**. The B checklist must contain only source-supported obligations, not hindsight from prior PR #45 mistakes or hidden grading expectations. The private grader and its expected outputs must never be accessible to either coding worker.
- Have a reviewer independent of the coding workers adjudicate all material source obligations and plausible alternatives **before** observing candidate implementations. Record identity/independence limitations honestly; no mere semantic certification from hashes or a model's self-assertion. Follow #36's source-to-oracle qualification and reject unsupported exception classes, exact wording/flag assumptions, or coverage gaps as valid defects.
- Apply the **same independent final acceptance assessment** to both arms: correct complete deliveries, genuinely missing source obligations, disputed/unknown requirements, unnecessary blocking, green-test omissions and resource consumption. Distinguish passed executable checks from unevaluated docs/usability obligations. Do not count an unavailable attempt as proven incorrect.
- Measure full elapsed time, model turns/tools, per-arm Luna input/cached/uncached/output tokens, normal self-tests, evaluator time, and **the time/tokens/human effort spent authoring, grounding, reviewing and distributing the checklist**. Preparation overhead is **not free** merely because it occurs before coding. Avoid cached-input double counting. Report dollars only when actually billed/observable; otherwise label actual billing **UNKNOWN** and present price-sensitivity separately.
- Compare *paired independently correct complete deliveries* and **total time/resources per correct delivery**. Describe small-N uncertainty and one-attempt variability. If both arms are all correct or too few defects appear, say **INCONCLUSIVE**. If checklist improves fidelity but overhead dominates, say so. Do not assume the checklist or Luna:medium is the optimal default.
- Make a plain **keep / simplify / reject / inconclusive** recommendation for this *minimal checklist only*, with specific evidence. Only after a useful advantage is observed should we separately evaluate whether Intentline's full `intentline-plan` offers *incremental* value worth its extra overhead, or whether optional Proofline feedback can recover an observed missed promise.

## Authorization and output

- **No live coding-model dispatch until a fresh, explicit, bounded user authorization** for this exact frozen cohort, effort setting, host and compute budget. Approval for #38 is not reusable; existing merge permissions are separate. No unsanctioned paid reviewer/authoring model calls.
- Keep published cohorts #16/#32/#34/#38 and their exposed candidates, grades and receipts immutable; do not pool old exposed results with this new study.
- Produce one compact PR with the predeclared protocol, checklist/source evidence, all-slot outcomes, independent acceptance assessment, token/time/cost accounting and an unembellished conclusion. **Do not merge without explicit user approval.**

## Definition of done

A **genuinely executed, small, matched and source-valid checklist-versus-ordinary Luna:medium study**, or a clearly documented authorized early stop/unavailable condition, with honest complete denominators and measured checklist overhead. No new production controller, mandatory planner, auditor, artificial rework loop or extensive benchmark infrastructure.

Related: [#38](https://github.com/grove/proofline/issues/38) remains an **incomplete medium/high study**; do not silently reopen its freeze, reuse its approval, or make this issue a continuation of the exposed #38 cohort.
title: Test whether concise acceptance guidance prevents Luna from missing user promises
